items.new_text: Load inbound rules with their conditions, ordered by `ordem` then ID exactly as `ordenarRegras` in `regra-fila.ts` evaluates them; a different screen order would make rule testing misleading. Include queues for the form and warn when a rule targets a disabled queue, which would swallow conversations.
A stored rule includes whether its destination queue is active, unlike the engine rule.
Inbox names and their default queue, used when no rule matches.
Use `fila_atendente.capacidade_override` or the queue default capacity.
This agent has an individual cap different from the queue default.

Store inbound rules here rather than in a Server Action: the frontend does not own the database (README, 'Quem fala com o banco — a fronteira'). This function accepts data and returns data without Next or JSX, so it can move to `apps/api` without a rewrite. `registrarAuditoria` in `@pipe/db` writes in the SAME transaction as the change; separate logging could disappear after a failed change or survive a rollback and misrepresent history.
`regra_fila` has no unique index on name; uniqueness is enforced by this
screen so duplicate 'Cobrança' rules cannot mislead a manager into editing the wrong one.

Inbound-rule REST writes add edit and delete to existing `gravarRegraFila` and `alternarAtivaDaRegraFila`. Use real `ErroPipe` statuses as in `editarFila`/`excluirFila`, not form `Resultado` in 200. Reordering is the `ordem` field of PATCH, with one PATCH per moved rule; `ordenarRegras` decides evaluation precedence. Conditions supplied in PATCH replace the prior set. This module stores the `ordem` number only; `ordenarRegras`/`filaDeDestino` in `regra-fila.ts` determines which matching rule wins first.
Only supplied fields change, as in `PedidoDeEdicaoDeFila`; supplied `condicoes` REPLACE all previous conditions.
Return this tenant's live rule with conditions, or 404.

Connect or disconnect a channel for a BOT, as source `/application/detail/{bot}/channels/{canal}` does behind 'Ativar número' (`FICHA-conectar-canal-no-bot.md` §§2,4). `fluxo.canal_id` was previously read by `fluxoPublicadoDoCanal`, while tests linked it by SQL; this adds the screen's write operation. Require `channels.escrever` on THIS flow or the account equivalent through `exigirPermissaoNoFluxo`. Reject a channel linked to another live bot, preserving the source's literal message 'Ops… Este número já está em uso / Para ativar o número neste bot, remova do anterior e tente novamente.' (`errorMsg.phoneNumberIsAlreadyConnected`); `detalhe` additionally identifies that bot. An inactive channel cannot receive, so linking returns 409. Pipe differs from Blip: `fluxo.canal_id` is one column, so this bot supports ONE channel; linking another returns 409 `fluxo_ja_tem_canal` rather than silently replacing WhatsApp, Messenger or Instagram.

Before creating a channel with `fluxo_id`, verify that the bot belongs to this tenant, the user may connect a channel to it, and it has no channel yet. Do not store client credentials only to reject the link afterward.
'Ativar número' links the channel to this bot; linking the same channel again is idempotent.
The title and message match the source's `whatsapp.errorMsg.phoneNumberIsAlreadyConnected`.

Disconnect the channel FROM THE BOT. The channel stays active; disconnecting the number itself (`DELETE /v1/canais/whatsapp/:id`) is a separate gesture. With no linked channel, make no change or audit entry. `motivo` comes from the source modal 'Por qual motivo você quer desconectar o …?' for Instagram/Messenger (`FICHA-conectar-canal-no-bot.md` §3.3); Blip uses it for analytics, while Pipe stores it in the audit log.

A bot administrator may reconnect THAT bot's channel after token expiry, as the source channel page permits. Return `true` only if the requested channel belongs to the bot and the user has authority there.
Return the live bot linked to this channel; archived bots do not reserve numbers.
Return a channel belonging to THIS tenant, or 404. Tenant identity comes from the session, never the request body.

Empty description becomes NULL because the form submits `''` when cleared. The source's `validateSpecialCharacter(description, 'description')` was not reproduced: its field-specific body was not observed, so using the name rule would be an assumption.

Identify an image by bytes, never its label. Return `null` for invalid content; creation may ignore it like source `uploadApplicationImageSafely`, while editing rejects it because `ng-mime-type` makes the source form invalid.
Check another LIVE contact with this name. An archived contact frees its name.

Ported from chatwoot/chatwoot (MIT), `app/controllers/api/v1/accounts/inboxes_controller.rb` (`create`, `update`, `destroy`, `avatar`) and `app/policies/inbox_policy.rb`. Contact (`fluxo` bot or router) lifecycle follows its Inbox sequence: authorize before create; fetch within account and authorize before update/delete; update supplied fields only; remove an avatar with `imagem: null`. Field rules come instead from Blip's Edit Flow DOM (`referencias-blip/portal/dom/application-detail-pipeprincipal-configurations-basic.html`) and creation wizard (`regras-de-nome.ts`): required name 2–30 starting with a letter; optional description 2–160 when present; optional image `.gif .png .jpeg .jpg` verified by BYTES. Source permissions also differ from Chatwoot: `automacao.fluxo.editar` (migration 0021) for create/edit, `automacao.fluxo.excluir` (migration 0023) for admin-only delete; the source says 'Somente um admin pode deletar o chatbot' (`deleteChatbotPermissionDenied`). Delete ARCHIVES here (`estado = 'arquivado'`) although Blip and Chatwoot permanently delete, because `execucao_fluxo.fluxo_versao_id` is `ON DELETE RESTRICT` and conversation history must remain for LGPD and contract obligations. Archived flows disappear from `carregarGradeDoPortal`, are ignored by `fluxoPublicadoDoCanal`, and free their name; this also permits restoration.
'Experimente usar outro nome' is the source's literal `errorMsg.1`.
`create` authorizes, validates and saves; invalid images are ignored as in the source.
Return the live contact or 404, like source `fetch_inbox`; archived contacts are treated as absent.
`update` changes supplied fields only; no change means no write and no audit entry.

'Configurações básicas' is a `PermissionsList.html` row (`basicConfigurations`), so a member with permission on THIS contact may edit it, alongside existing account-level permission (`exigirPermissaoNoFluxo`, migration 0035).
`destroy` archives the contact, removing it from the list and channel for the reason in the file header.
Only supplied fields change: `undefined` means leave unchanged; `null` means clear.

Use `regras-de-nome.ts` for names on create and edit: source `validateSpecialCharacter` and `<input>` attributes are the same on both screens. `conferir` returns the FIRST rejection as a code; `ErroPipe` owns the user-facing sentence.
`variaveis` is unchecked `jsonb`; one corrupt row must not break the whole list.
From catalog migration 0030: no earlier permission covered quick replies.

Communication reads for quick replies and WhatsApp message templates. `resposta_pronta.atalho` has an `index`, not `uniqueIndex`; `salvarRespostaPronta` in `app/comunicacao/acoes.ts` checks tenant conflicts before insert within its transaction. `resposta_pronta.escopo` distinguishes company replies managed here from personal replies created in Desk (see `2026-09-05-desk-requisitos.md` §5 and `estrutura-gestao.tsx`); this screen lists and creates only `escopo = 'empresa'`.
Only WhatsApp channels have message templates through the Cloud API.

Quick-reply REST writes add edit and delete to existing `salvarRespostaPronta` creation. Follow `ciclo-de-vida-do-fluxo.ts` with real `ErroPipe` statuses; retain the older form `acoes/*` `Resultado` in 200 for its existing callers.
`resposta_pronta.atalho` has `index`, not `uniqueIndex`; enforce tenant uniqueness in this function before `insert`/`update`, not through a database constraint.
Leave the type unannotated: the inferred literal satisfies `Record<string, unknown>` in `diferenca`.

Only a MEDIA header uses send position 1. `apps/workers/src/whatsapp/template.ts` uses the same rule when sending; cross-app imports are unavailable, so keep this calculation aligned to warn at registration before production delivery fails.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.
Both source screens use `basicConfigurations` in `PermissionsList.html`; a member with permission on THIS contact may save, alongside existing account-level permission (migration 0035).

Welcome Screen ('Tela de Boas-vindas') and Persistent Menu ('Menu Persistente') are source `/configurations/*` items 2 and 3 (`referencias-blip/pesquisa/blip-portal-telas.md` §6), stored in `fluxo.configuracao` since migration 0031. Earlier forms had no persistence. Active source fields were not observed because enabling the production router would change its state (`boasvindas/tela.tsx`), so no source limit was captured for 'Mensagem de saudação'. Pipe chose 20 characters for 'Texto do botão' based on Messenger `quick_replies[].title`. Both PATCHes require `automacao.fluxo.editar`, as editing a contact does in `servicos-do-roteador.ts`.
Verify with a real token that the Page accepts this combination of `get_started` and `greeting`.
A filled welcome screen is active with message and button text; the persistent menu requires it.

Enforce both source gates: a connected Messenger channel and a populated Welcome Screen (`tela.tsx`). The earlier source note said the second gate could not yet be reproduced; Welcome Screen is now persisted.
Both source screens use `basicConfigurations` in `PermissionsList.html`; a member with permission on THIS contact may save, alongside existing account-level permission (migration 0035).
Verify with a real token that the Page accepts this `persistent_menu` shape.
Return this account's live flow with raw configuration, or 404.
Require and read these fields only when `ativo` is `true`.

`ativo: false` disables without erasing saved content, so reactivation restores the prior message. For an active Messenger contact, also update the Page profile (`get_started`/`greeting`); local persistence remains the screen's read source.

`carregarOperacao` left with `/configuracoes/operacao`. Its agent grid became `carregarAtendentes` in `cadastros.ts` with missing queue/capacity columns; pause reasons now have an editing form in `/atendentes/pausas`.

Channels are a module in the source navigation rather than preference data. Include the inbox because it, not the carrier channel, owns the default queue. Distinguishing the two prevents seeking queue settings on the WhatsApp screen. Count OPEN conversations, not lifetime history, to show whether the channel is currently delivering.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.
Use one query for all inboxes and group in memory. Avoid `Promise.all` inside this transaction: parallel queries on one connection can lose the RLS session variable.

Reuse catalog permission 'Configurar marca, fuso e plano' for General Settings writes to identity, survey and closing labels; before the Attendance registration task (item 7), none had permission checks.

General Settings reads supply writable forms, unlike the read-only sections above. Each configuration card saves independently, matching `blip-telas-cadastro.md` §3: 'em Configurações gerais não há um botão Salvar da tela'.
The tenant's active survey, or `null` if none has been configured.
Count other surveys because spec §6 requires one scale per survey.
Show the most recently configured survey for editing and the count of others. Hiding duplicates could combine different scales in one chart.

Read and write tenant configuration here. Editing requires audit of actor, prior value and time; `registrarAuditoria` in `@pipe/db` now writes in the SAME transaction as the change, so rollback cannot leave a misleading log. This module accepts data and returns data without Next, `revalidatePath` or JSX, allowing it to move into `apps/api` without a rewrite (README, 'Quem fala com o banco').

Tenant configuration writes live here, not in a Server Action: the frontend does not own the database (README, 'Quem fala com o banco'). Each function accepts and returns data and calls `registrarAuditoria` with its `tx` in the SAME transaction to keep log and data consistent. `diferenca` records changed fields only, so the audit shows the actual time-zone change rather than unchanged columns.
Use `type`, not `interface`: only the alias gets the implicit index signature needed for `diferenca` to accept it as `Record<string, unknown>`.

The checked closing labels replace the whole required list: checked labels become required, unchecked labels stop being required. Merely adding checked labels would make the policy impossible to undo from the screen.
Audit the tenant-wide closing policy, not an individual label; `antes` and `depois` record which names entered and left the list.
Database labels are ordinary Portuguese, but the target is an enum rather than free text.

Read and write the contract panel (`/contrato`). Like `lib/configuracoes.ts`, this module accepts parameters and returns data without Next, `revalidatePath` or JSX, so it can move to an `apps/api` endpoint without a rewrite (README, 'Quem fala com o banco'). Screen reference: `referencias-blip/pesquisa/blip-painel-do-contrato.md`.
Offer only the three account roles in Members and Invite. Manager, supervisor, agent and evaluator are attendance roles assigned per contact in the source.

List people with account access and pending invitees together. Only active users count: `removerMembro` deactivates instead of deleting, preserving names in conversations, evaluations and audit logs. Source invitees are `tenant-user` rows with `userStatus: 'PendingUser'`, shown with '(Pendente)'; expired invites grant no access and accepted ones are already users, so exclude both. An invitee has no name before first sign-in; display the email prefix, matching source fallback `decodeURIComponent(userIdentity.split('@')[0])`.
Join the single ACCOUNT role per user (migration 0021 partial index), so the row is not multiplied; attendance roles belong to another screen.
The account role that the source calls `admin`; see `PAPEIS_DA_ORIGEM`.
Count active ACCOUNT administrators only. A deactivated admin no longer has access, so must not satisfy the last-admin guard.

Replace one member's ACCOUNT role in a single transaction: remove the old role before adding the new, matching the source's single `roleId`. Leave attendance roles untouched, so changing account Admin to view-only does not remove attendance access. Audit both values.
Demoting the LAST active admin would remove the only account able to
grant that role again, leaving the contract unmanaged.
Write creation dates in the account time zone, not the server time zone.

Remove a contract member by DEACTIVATING, never deleting. `usuario` is referenced by conversations, evaluations, leads and audit records; deleting it would erase attribution needed by contract audits. `ativo = false` already blocks sign-in (`packages/autenticacao/src/entrada.ts`). Keep the role so a reactivated member returns to their former responsibilities.
Source 'Chatbots' card counts live flows and routers, excluding archived ones.
Source 'Membros' card counts only people who still have access.
